Scale and detail

Small patterns should prioritize head, markings and outline. On a cow, spot distribution can add identity; on a sheep, the wool mass needs enough contrast to avoid becoming one white block.

Work in stitch dimensions rather than pixels alone. The same artwork may work at 120 stitches wide and lose its identity completely when reduced to 45. Color and style

A farm composition can mix several animals, but scale needs control so none appears accidentally enormous. A shared ground line or framing system helps maintain visual proportion.

Limit colors deliberately. Every extra shade should add volume, separation or identity; if it appears in only a few stitches without changing the image, it may add work rather than quality. Composition and personalization

Cream, green, terracotta and black can create a contemporary rural palette; pop colors can move the same theme toward kitchens, children's rooms or more graphic decor.
